summary: L2Solo is a standalone, local-first Lineage II Chronicle 4 (C4 "Scions of Destiny", protocol 656) server emulator written in Node.js (>=22.5), built as a heavily modified fork of the NodeL2 emulator, licensed Apache-2.0. Its explicit purpose is a single-player/solo MMO: one real player in a world populated by up to ~1,700 AI-driven bots across hot/cold/static tiers. Critically, it ALREADY contains a mature, LLM-driven bot brain with persona traits, tool-style structured decisions, multi-layer inference budgeting, LOD/proximity gating, and a scripted FSM fallback layer â€” this is exactly the kind of layer our project wants. It is NOT L2J/Mobius-based (pure JS, in-process simulated actors, no fake network clients), so it cannot be code-merged into a Java Mobius core; it is an alternative architecture to adopt-from or port, not a drop-in module.
key_facts: Identity: 'Lineage II Chronicle 4 server emulator tuned for a solo MMO experience. Smart bots, aiming to a complete offline simulation.' Status: public alpha ('Work in progress. Playable.'). Topics include ai-bot, ai-player, l2c4, lineage2-solo, solo-mmo, nodejs.
Chronicle/version: C4 'Scions of Destiny', client protocol 656. Explicitly NOT Interlude and NOT High Five.

Language/runtime: Node.js (engines.node >= 22.5.0), package name 'nodel2' v0.0.7, author Dennis Koluris (the original NodeL2 author). Database is SQLite; config via INI files (config/default.ini, config/local.ini); geodata is a downloaded C4 pack (~900MiB).

Server integration: FULLY STANDALONE. Described as a heavily modified solo-MMO fork of the NodeL2 Server Emulator. It is its own game+auth server (src/AuthenticationServer, src/GameServer, src/Packet, src/WorldObserver). It is NOT built on L2J or Mobius and has no Java.

Bots are IN-PROCESS simulated actors, NOT fake network clients. Each bot gets a BotSession whose session.actor is the same character-object type used by real players (enterWorld(), fetchHp(), etc.); real players drive their actor via network packets, bots drive theirs via BotAI. Filtered from player ops via accountId startsWith 'bot_'. (src/GameServer/Bot/BotManager.js)

YES it contains a full fake-player/AI-companion system. Bot code lives in src/GameServer/Bot with subdirs AI, Economy, Goals, LoadTest, Population, Simulation and files BotManager.js, BotPopulation.js, BotSession.js, BotAI.js, BotMerchant.js, BotClassProgression.js, TradeService.js.

Bot intelligence is a HYBRID, not purely scripted. Core decisions are LLM-driven: BotBrain.js (~600-650 lines) calls requestDecision -> OpenRouterGateway.request with a system prompt + JSON context payload and a STRICT JSON response schema (required fields action, reply, reason, confidence). A scripted FSM exists as the fallback/behavioral layer: src/GameServer/Bot/AI/States/ has FleeingState, FollowingState, GettingBuffedState, HuntingState, MerchantState, PkFleeingState, PkHuntingState, RestingState, ShoppingState. Party-command overrides are hardcoded rules (applyPartyPolicy).
Goal system: src/GameServer/Bot/Goals has GoalExecutor.js, GoalPlanner.js, GoalService.js, GoalState.js, NeedsEvaluator.js â€” a goal-oriented planning layer above the states.

LLM gateway (src/GameServer/Bot/AI/OpenRouterGateway.js): dual-mode, auto-detects OpenRouter (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions) vs any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama/LM Studio). NON-streaming POST (response.json()). Uses response_format json_schema (strict) for structured output. NO OpenAI tool/function-calling fields are sent â€” structured output only via JSON schema. Defaults: maxTokens 320, timeoutMs 3500, temperature 0.35, reasoningEffort 'low', maxConcurrentRequests 32. Has a circuit breaker and schema-repair/retry-with-doubled-budget. Config layered: defaults -> INI [AI]/legacy [OpenRouter] -> env (L2NODE_AI_* / OPENROUTER_*) -> per-call.

No 'openai'/'langchain' SDK dependency â€” LLM calls are raw HTTP. Dependencies include @langfuse/otel and @langfuse/tracing (^5.10.0) plus @opentelemetry/sdk-node for LLM observability (LangfuseTracing.js).

Persona system (src/GameServer/Bot/AI/BotPersona.js): 7 numeric traits 0.0-1.0 [sociability, commitment, caution, ambition, assertiveness, empathy, resilience], deterministically seeded from characterId, with a primary drive [progression, wealth, social] and archetypes (e.g. steady_achiever, pragmatic_earner). Derives textCard (prose) + dialogueVoice fed into LLM prompts. Persisted to SQLite table bot_personas (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(characterId) DO NOTHING).

Scale gating: BotInferenceBudget.js enforces dual sliding-window (60s) limits â€” per-bot: 6 requests, 12000 prompt tokens, 2400 completion tokens; global: 240 requests, 300000 prompt tokens, 64000 completion tokens, 32 concurrent, 256 queued waiters. On exhaustion it returns rejection reason codes + retryAfterMs (no built-in scripted fallback in that module; caller decides).

LOD gating: HotActorLodPolicy.js â€” three tiers full/visible/preload by distance to real player: full <=3500 units (tick ~3s, ~1s if high-risk <=1200), visible <=6000 (tick 7s, 6ms budget), preload beyond (tick 30s). Hysteresis 3500-4000. 8s promotion hold when targeted/damaged/in party/clan quest/trade/combat. NO hard cap on number of hot bots in this module.

Dispatch: HotAiDispatcher.js is a single-task-at-a-time coalescing queue (one pending task per bot key; duplicate requests coalesced; urgent queue processed first) â€” it prevents LLM-call floods but does NOT itself select which bots are eligible (that is upstream: LOD + budget).

Population reality vs README: BotPopulation.buildStarterBots() hardcodes only ~65 STATIC starter bots (5 villages x 13) plus PkProfiles.materializeBots(); the '~1,700 bots' is a runtime population target managed by PopulationService/SimulationKernel with cold bots costing no runtime until activated (markHot/cooldownSession). SimulationKernel.js is a module-orchestration/event-routing system (default event drain limit 50), not a per-frame population ticker.
License: Apache License 2.0 (generic template, no filled-in copyright owner in the LICENSE file).
npm scripts confirm bot maturity: wipe:bots, load:mixed (mixed-runtime-load-test.js), and a Bot/LoadTest/ subdirectory exist for scale testing.
architecture_notes: Our target (L2J Mobius, Java) and L2Solo (Node.js) are different runtimes and codebases â€” there is NO code-level merge path. L2Solo's bot layer cannot be dropped into a Java Mobius core as-is. The realistic options are: (a) PORT its bot-brain design/algorithms into Java, or (b) run L2Solo's bot logic as an external Node.js sidecar that a Mobius bridge talks to, or (c) treat L2Solo as design reference and build our own layer.

L2Solo's architecture is a strong reference blueprint for '5000 human-like LLM fake players.' The layering it already solved is exactly our hard problem: LOD/proximity tiering (HotActorLodPolicy) + dual per-bot/global inference budgets (BotInferenceBudget) + a coalescing single-flight dispatcher (HotAiDispatcher) + LLM-driven structured decisions (BotBrain + OpenRouterGateway json_schema) with a scripted FSM fallback (AI/States). We should reuse this decomposition regardless of language.

Key insight for scale: L2Solo does NOT run an LLM per bot per tick. Only 'full'/hot bots near the single player think, gated to a global 240 LLM requests/60s. For our 5000-bot goal this is the critical lesson â€” LLM cost is bounded by a small active-attention window plus budget caps, and the vast majority of bots run cheap scripted/goal-based simulation. Any Mobius port must replicate this hot/cold tiering or LLM cost will be prohibitive.

L2Solo is single-real-player-centric: LOD tiers are computed relative to THE player. Our multi-player-observed or many-hot-region scenario would need the eligibility logic generalized (multiple attention centers), which is upstream of HotAiDispatcher and would be the main adaptation area.
Bots-as-in-process-actors (not fake clients) matches how Mobius internally represents NPCs/players too, so the conceptual model ports cleanly to a Java core even though the code does not.

The LLM integration is provider-agnostic (OpenAI-compatible) and uses structured JSON output rather than function-calling â€” a portable, model-neutral contract we can mirror in Java (e.g. via a thin HTTP client).
risks: Language/architecture mismatch is the biggest risk: L2Solo is Node.js + SQLite + C4 protocol 656, our target is Java L2J Mobius. Direct merge is impossible; any adoption is a port or a sidecar integration, both non-trivial engineering efforts.

Chronicle mismatch: L2Solo is hardcoded to C4 (protocol 656, C4 geodata, C4 skill coverage). If our Mobius project is a different chronicle (Interlude/High Five/Classic etc.), skill IDs, formulas, item tables, and packet structures differ â€” bot combat/skill logic would need retargeting.

Scale evidence gap: the '~1,700 bots' and '5000' goals are runtime targets; the repo hardcodes only ~65 static starter bots and provides load-test scripts (LoadTest/, mixed-runtime-load-test.js). There is no proof in-tree that thousands of concurrently LLM-active bots run smoothly; hot-bot LLM concurrency is deliberately capped low (32 concurrent / 240 req per 60s).
Public alpha maturity: README says 'Work in progress'; APIs and data schemas may be unstable. Version 0.0.7.
No function/tool-calling in the LLM gateway (json_schema only) â€” if our design assumes tool-use agents, we'd extend or replace the gateway.
Single-player-centric LOD assumption may not fit a design where 5000 bots must appear human-like to many observers or across many regions simultaneously.

Apache-2.0 is permissive and merge-friendly legally, BUT L2J/Mobius cores are typically GPL-family; mixing an Apache-2.0 Node project's design is fine, but copying any code into a GPL Java project has the usual one-directional-compatibility caveats â€” here it's moot since there's no shared language, but license hygiene matters if any assets/data are reused.
recommendations: Treat L2Solo as a DESIGN REFERENCE / architecture blueprint to ADAPT, not a module to merge â€” because it is Node.js/C4 and our target is Java/Mobius. There is no code-merge path.

Port L2Solo's proven control-plane decomposition into our Mobius bot layer: LOD tiering (hot/cold/static), dual per-bot + global inference budgets with sliding windows, a coalescing single-flight LLM dispatcher, and structured-JSON LLM decisions with a scripted-FSM/goal fallback. These four pieces are the reusable IP.

Do NOT plan one LLM call per bot per tick. Adopt L2Solo's model: only a bounded 'attention window' of hot bots think via LLM; the other ~thousands run cheap goal/FSM simulation. This is the make-or-break design for a 5000-bot budget.

Reuse the persona model concept directly: 7 numeric traits + primary drive + archetype -> prose 'textCard' + 'dialogueVoice' injected into prompts, persisted per character. It's simple, deterministic, and portable to Java.

If a Java port is too costly near-term, consider a SIDECAR: run L2Solo's (or a stripped bot-brain extracted from it) as a Node.js service that our Mobius server queries over IPC/HTTP for high-level decisions, while Mobius executes them on real NPC/player objects. This reuses the actual code but decouples runtimes.

Confirm our project's chronicle first. If it's not C4, budget for retargeting skill/formula/item logic; the AI control-plane ports regardless but the game-mechanics-aware pieces (combat, skills, gear) are chronicle-specific.
Generalize the LOD 'attention center' from single-player to multi-center before scaling, since L2Solo assumes one real player.
Extend the LLM gateway design with real tool/function-calling if our agents need it â€” L2Solo currently uses json_schema structured output only.
open_questions: What chronicle is OUR L2J Mobius project on? This determines how much game-mechanics porting (skills/formulas/items) the bot layer needs; the AI control-plane ports regardless.

What is the actual measured concurrency ceiling for LLM-active bots in L2Solo under load (the LoadTest/ and mixed-runtime-load-test.js results)? Needed to validate feasibility of thousands of simultaneously 'human-like' bots.

Does our 5000-bot vision require many bots to be LLM-active at once (many observers/regions), or is a small attention window acceptable? This decides whether L2Solo's single-player LOD model is sufficient or must be reworked.
Is a Java port acceptable, or would a Node.js sidecar bridge to Mobius be preferred? Determines whether we reuse code or only design.

How much of L2Solo's cold-bot 'background simulation' (economy, clans, goals) do we want â€” the Population/Simulation/Economy subsystems were not deeply inspected and may be substantial additional value or additional porting cost.

What is our target LLM provider/model and per-hour token budget? L2Solo defaults are tiny (320 max tokens, low reasoning) â€” our human-like quality bar may require larger budgets, changing the cost math.
